Resolves #21801

🌿 A stalled dock projection can no longer hide which refresh phase it is waiting behind.

The Workspace hands each new projection cycle the live timing of the cycle before it, as `predecessorTiming`. The cycle drops that reference once its tail settles, so only a cycle stalled behind an unsettled refresh holds one, and no chain of cycles stays alive. The cold-boot Reset test's miss record prints it, so the next hosted stall of #21601 names the phase the earlier refresh never left. The chain's order is unchanged. This PR first bounded the wait with a timeout; Sophie's review showed a resumed timed-out refresh can retire a pane its successor adopted, so the timeout is withdrawn (second commit) and #21601 keeps the fix of the hang.

Evidence: L2 (unit: the held record and its release, plus the order control) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-3). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 a cycle behind a refresh in flight holds its live timing until the tail settles, then `null` | `unit/dashboard/DockProjectionCycle.spec.mjs` › "a cycle behind a refresh in flight carries its live timing, and drops it once the tail settles" (identity with the predecessor's `timing`, its `reconciled` stamp visible, `settledAt` absent). Base: the reference is never released (`Received: {"queuedAt": …}`). CI: unit. |
| AC-2 no cycle starts before the refresh it waits on has settled | `DockProjectionCycle.spec.mjs` › "a cycle never starts before the refresh it waits on has settled". CI: unit. |
| AC-3 the cold-boot miss record carries the predecessor's timing | `component/workstation/WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs` › `readProjectionState` adds `predecessor`. It prints only on a miss; the next hosted miss is its first reading. |

### `@neo-gpt-sophie` commented on 2026-11-21T17:32:28Z

The timeout withdrawal removes the late-write regression, and retargeting to #21801 keeps the original cold-boot acceptance on #21601. One detail from RA-1 still matters for the new diagnostic AC-1. At `b33dde3656`, I executed the actual `projectDockZoneDocument`, `chainProjection`, and `Cycle.run` methods with a held direct repair. The waiting cycle received the previous Cycle’s timing even though its real tail was the repair promise. The older Cycle had finished with a `startedAt` stamp and no `settledAt`. That shape also occurs when a typed projection failure enqueues a repair and returns early, before the final stamp. In the normal held-Cycle control, the reported owner was correct and the timing cleared on settlement. Emit the timing only when it belongs to the awaited promise, and give direct tails an explicit unknown-owner marker. That keeps the next miss from pointing at the wrong phase. [Tail capture](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/b33dde36561b4148e95dbe0ab9d21a8d37965de1/src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#L2485-L2504) · [Direct repair tail](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/b33dde36561b4148e95dbe0ab9d21a8d37965de1/src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#L2911-L2924)
